facts.title: About Manoj
facts.text: Manoj Mathivanan is a software architect based in Chennai, India. His work focuses on distributed systems, messaging and streaming, automation, and connected devices. Career information is documented through October 2026, with Staff Software Engineer recorded in the 2025 PayPal review. Do not infer employment or availability beyond the documented cutoff.

facts.title: PayPal experience
facts.text: Staff Software Engineer · Kafka Platform at PayPal. February 2021 – documented through October 2026 · Member of Technical Staff 1, then Member of Technical Staff 2 / Staff Software Engineer. Technical leadership across Kafka architecture, cloud modernization, reliability, and AI-assisted operations. 2026: Architected and delivered production Kafka on GKE using Strimzi, Helm, and Harness. Defined clusters, topics, ACLs, and configuration as code, with validation, rollback, and audit trails. Cut provisioning from about three days to under 15 minutes. 2026: Designed and built an autoscaling SNI-routing gateway with one entry IP per GKE cluster and end-to-end mTLS; designed highly available discovery and co-authored a cloud migration strategy accepted by the Cloud Architecture Forum. 2026: Built and tested automatic client re-bootstrap for cluster moves without application restarts. Producer switching took about 1–2 seconds and consumer switching 5–10 seconds in tests, with no message loss in three scenarios. Client rollout remained pending in October 2026. 2025–2026: Designed and deployed the Kafka MCP server, then extended its tools and integrated Slack-based troubleshooting. Built a Slack-triggered agentic AI assistant using LangGraph and Claude, combining MCP tools with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to answer queries and support Kafka troubleshooting. Estimated data collection and analysis fell from at least two hours to under two minutes; the 2026 bot handled 10 customer issues and 50+ internal queries. 2024–2025: Led the redesign and deployment of MirrorMaker 2 from VM-based replication to a Kubernetes-based platform; integrated authentication, observability, management UIs, and secure production-to-sandbox mirroring. 2024: Led a phased SASL security rollout with no user impact reported in the review, and completed migration of Kafka observability from SignalFx to Datadog using Micrometer. 2025: Contributed an Apache Kafka performance-testing fix for large payload files (KAFKA-18115, PR #18391), merged into the upstream project in May 2025. 2023: Rebuilt the Kafka QA platform with Terraform, Ansible, Docker, and Puppet. Reduced monthly infrastructure cost from about $39,000 to $4,000 and cluster installation from hours to five minutes, with production-aligned test environments. 2021–2022: Led Kafka infrastructure and disaster-recovery setup for the China payments environment; built partition-aware failover automation, cross-region metadata synchronization, and container-aware patching. Migrated the cluster metadata repository without downtime or data loss. 2025–2026: Automated fleet upgrades and change workflows, mentored engineers, led design reviews and sprint planning, and covered interim team management in 2025. In 2026, planned and groomed 351 stories for five engineers; about 80% were closed at the summary date. These curated facts combine earlier resumes and 2021–2026 impact summaries; career cutoff is October 2026.

facts.title: SAP Labs experience
facts.text: Associate Development Architect at SAP Labs. March 2012 – February 2021. Cloud frameworks, data services, and developer tools. Role progression: Quality Associate – Performance (March 2012–October 2014); Developer (August 2013–October 2014 and November 2014–March 2016); Senior Developer (March 2016–March 2019); Associate Development Architect (March 2019–February 2021). Worked with a research team in Germany on database-independent Core Data Services (CDS) modeling and exposure through the OData protocol. Developed a Java annotation-based extension framework that let SAP cloud developers expose HANA databases as OData services with minimal coding. Built a multi-tenant enterprise backend-as-a-service application using Java, Node.js, and SAP UI5 to provision databases, deploy models, and expose REST services with minimal application code. Created a framework for end-to-end REST service testing with record and playback support. Shared knowledge with the developer community through talks and workshops at SAP Tech Hub. In a performance engineering role, built mobile test apps for Android, iOS, and BlackBerry and used Introscope to capture performance results. Automated tests reduced a two-hour workflow to ten minutes. These curated facts combine earlier resumes and 2021–2026 impact summaries; career cutoff is October 2026.
facts.keywords: SAP Labs Associate Development Architect Java OData Developer frameworks Performance experience work career job employment
